critical_code_review_comments: server.py::client_ip returns request.client.host (which is the proxy IP inside k8s) as ultimate fallback when neither x-real-ip nor x-forwarded-for is set. In a preview environment the proxy always injects one of these, but if the app is ever deployed behind a proxy that strips both headers, all traffic collapses to the same source IP and per-IP rate limiting effectively becomes a global limiter. Acceptable defense-in-depth given the additional CONTACT_GLOBAL_LIMIT, but worth documenting the trust boundary.

server.py rate-limit uses count_documents with an in-memory 'window_start' filter alongside a Mongo TTL index on created_at (expireAfterSeconds=CONTACT_RATE_WINDOW_SEC). This is correct but slightly redundant; the TTL sweep runs every 60s so occasional counts can include documents up to ~60s past the window, marginally over-counting. Non-blocking.

server.py security_headers is registered as an app middleware AFTER app.include_router(api_router). FastAPI/Starlette registers middleware in reverse of the actual runtime chain, so this works today, but adding another middleware later in the file without matching CORS registration order could reorder in surprising ways. Consider grouping middleware registration in a single block near app creation.

ServicePage.jsx ServiceContactForm hard-codes text-cink/bg-cwhite (correct fix), but the Field wrapper label at line ~388 uses text-cink/50 — the browser computed value in our test came back as null for span discovery due to selector, but visually the labels are legible in both themes (confirmed by screenshots). No action needed.
